validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently documented FERC NGA section 7(c) proceeding, not a GEM-only entity. Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT) filed an abbreviated application on 2021-01-29 in Docket CP21-45-000 seeking authority to construct, own, and operate the 'Big Bend Project' -- two segments of 36-inch mainline loop extension totaling 3.2 miles plus pig-receiver relocations in Calhoun and Jefferson Counties, FL, and an 8,000 HP compressor uprate across CS 12/14/15/24 in Santa Rosa, Gadsden, Taylor and Gilchrist Counties, FL (Federal Register 2021-03370, govinfo PDF, verified live via url_verifier). Corroborated independently by EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' workbook (row 'Big Bend Project', Pipeline Operator Name 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Docket CP21-45, Miles 3.2, Diameter 36, Capacity 29 MMcf/d, Cost $38M, States FL/FL/FL) and by ECB Publishing's local Jefferson County newspaper coverage (Lazaro Aleman, 2021-04-01, ecbpublishing.com, verified live), which independently reports the same filing date, cost ($37,527,398) and county-level scope from its own reading of the FERC docket. Not GEM-only; three independent-origin documents (FERC's own Federal Register notices, EIA's federal dataset, and independent local press) agree. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas is correct -- this is an NGA section 7(c) natural gas pipeline certificate proceeding start to finish; no classification concern. The project is a loop-extension/expansion, but unlike the sheet's LengthKnown=0 rule for no-new-pipe expansions, Big Bend genuinely adds new physical pipe (3.2 mi / 5.15 km of new 36-inch loop, per the FERC application), so LengthKnown=5.10 km (recorded) correctly stays non-zero -- this is NOT a compression-only or metering-only scope. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 44-row Gulf Coast in-development roster. Per the batch's own duplicate/family guidance, P3192 (FGT Big Bend) is a singleton alongside P7824 (FGT South Central Louisiana) and P5548 (FGT South Louisiana, in a parallel batch) -- all three are distinct FGT system projects with different scopes/counties/dockets; Big Bend's docket CP21-45-000 and Calhoun/Jefferson/Santa Rosa/Gadsden/Taylor/Gilchrist County FL scope do not overlap with either. No relabel/double-count found. status_reviews.researcher_notes: The question for this cancelled row is whether the cancellation is right and sourced, not whether it is dormant (per batch guidance). It is: FERC's own 'Notice of Effectiveness of Withdrawal of Application' (Federal Register 2022-06805, govinfo PDF, Docket CP21-45-000) states that FGT filed its application on 2021-01-29 'for authorization to construct, own, and operate its Big Bend Project', that FGT filed a notice of withdrawal on 2022-02-22, no motion opposed it, and 'the withdrawal of the application became effective on March 10, 2022, and this proceeding is hereby terminated.' This is a discrete, dated, primary regulatory record of cancellation -- not a dormancy inference -- so ShelvedCancelledType should read 'confirmed' rather than 'inferred' (recommending the change since the batch's default assumption for these three cancelled rows is an existing 'inferred' tag; if the sheet already reads 'confirmed' this proposed_changes entry is a no-op confirmation). Independently corroborated by EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Historical Projects tab), whose 'Big Bend Project' row shows Status='Cancelled' with Last Updated Date 2022-03-25 -- 15 days after FERC's withdrawal became effective, consistent with EIA updating its dataset off the same docket termination. CancelledYear=2022 (recorded) matches both the withdrawal's effective date (2022-03-10) and EIA's update date exactly -- no correction needed. Searched federalregister.gov directly (returns HTTP 500 on this document type -- a server-side issue, not a bot-block; used the govinfo.gov PDF mirror instead, which returns 200), FERC eLibrary docket CP21-45 listing, and general press (Tampa Bay Times, ECB Publishing, NGI) for any later news of a revival or re-filing under a new docket; none found. No evidence the project was ever built under a different name -- Big Bend does not reappear in TECO's or FGT's later system-expansion announcements (e.g. the 2025-2026 FGT Phase 9 expansion covered by NaturalGasIntel, which does not mention Big Bend). This is the newest and most authoritative evidence found (2022-03), and no independent news postdates it, so status remains cancelled with high confidence.
